# Phase 01.1: Code Review Report

**Reviewed:** 2026-08-05T08:40:00Z
**Depth:** standard
**Files Reviewed:** 76
**Status:** issues_found

> **Notation warning — read before editing this file.** This document lives under
> `.planning/`, which Tailwind v4 currently scans as *source* (that is finding
> CR-01). Every Tailwind arbitrary-value class quoted below therefore has the
> contents of its square brackets replaced with a CAPITALISED PLACEHOLDER, so
> that quoting the defect does not re-create it. The substitution is named at
> each site. **Do not "restore" the real literals into this file.**

## Summary

The implementation quality inside `app/`, `components/`, `lib/` and `actions/` is
high. The contrast engine in `lib/theme/contrast.ts` is correct against WCAG 2.1
including the blue-channel linearisation the research snippet got wrong; the
token indirection in `app/globals.css` is sound; the Supabase error-channel
discipline in `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` and `lib/venue-page-read.ts` is
genuinely careful; the touch-floor mechanism in `button.tsx` / `checkbox.tsx` /
`radio-group.tsx` computes to a real 44px.

That is not what is wrong with this phase.

**The application does not start.** Every route returns HTTP 500 under
`pnpm dev`, because the *stylesheet* is being assembled from inputs that no gate
in this repo polices. Tailwind v4's automatic source detection is scanning the
entire repository — including 499 committed markdown files and a design-bundle
preview directory — and compiling backticked class literals out of *prose* into
the app's real CSS. One of those prose literals contains an author's ellipsis
placeholder, which produces an unparseable `var()` reference, which takes down
`app/globals.css`, which takes down `app/layout.tsx`, which takes down every page.

Two facts make this worse than one bad line of markdown:

1. **`pnpm build` passes.** The identical defect surfaces there only as a
   non-fatal `Found 1 warning while optimizing generated CSS` line. A green build
   is currently *not* evidence that the application runs. Any verification step
   that treats `next build` as proof of life is reporting a false pass on a total
   outage.
2. **It has already happened more than once.** Grepping the generated CSS in
   `.next/` proves that at least seven arbitrary-value utilities in the shipped
   stylesheet have no origin anywhere in `app/`, `components/`, `lib/` or
   `actions/`. They come from a planning SUMMARY, from `.design-sync/NOTES.md`,
   from `.design-sync/conventions.md` and from `.design-sync/previews/*.tsx`. One
   emits a syntactically invalid `border-radius` declaration into production CSS
   today. Another injects a font size the phase's own four-role typography
   contract forbids — and `tests/theme/design-system-discipline.test.ts` cannot
   see it, because that gate scans three directories while the compiler scans the
   repository.

The remaining findings are ordinary: an unmounted `next-themes` provider that
silently hands the toast system OS-driven dark mode in a product that explicitly
forbids OS-driven dark mode; two primitives that opted out of the reduced-motion
contract the token layer claims to enforce for everyone; discarded Supabase error
channels that contradict the discipline applied two files away; a form that can
render unsubmittable with no message; and a handful of stale comments and dead
tokens.

---

## Critical Issues

### CR-01: Tailwind compiles a planning document into invalid CSS; every route 500s in dev

**File:** `app/globals.css:1` (the bare `@import "tailwindcss"`)
**Also implicates:** `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-10-SUMMARY.md:28`, `.gitignore`

**Reproduction (confirmed in this working tree):**

```
pnpm build   -> SUCCEEDS. TypeScript passes. All 12 routes generate.
pnpm dev     -> starts, but:
  curl localhost:3000/        -> 500
  curl localhost:3000/login   -> 500
  curl localhost:3000/venues  -> 500
```

**The error**, from `.next/dev/logs/next-development.log` (9 occurrences across
3 dev sessions, verified present):

```
./app/globals.css:556:40
Parsing CSS source code failed
  555 |   .max-h-\[min\(20rem\,var\(--radix-\.\.\.-available-height\)\)\] {
> 556 |     max-height: min(20rem, var(--radix-...-available-height));
      |                                        ^
Unexpected token Delim('.')

Import trace:
  Client Component Browser:
    ./app/globals.css [Client Component Browser]
    ./app/layout.tsx [Server Component]
```

**Issue.** `app/globals.css` is 311 lines long. Line 556 does not exist in the
source — it is in Tailwind's *generated* output. Tailwind v4 manufactured that
utility from a string it scanned out of a committed planning document:

```
.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-10-SUMMARY.md:28
  - "Doubly-bounded overlay height: `max-h-[min(20rem,var(--radix-ELLIPSIS-available-height))]`
     keeps both a fixed ceiling and Radix's measured space in ONE twMerge group"
```

*(ELLIPSIS stands in for three literal ASCII full stops in the real file. It is
an author's shorthand for "dropdown-menu-content" / "select-content" / etc. It is
not a CSS custom property, and it is the only occurrence of that literal anywhere
outside `node_modules/` and `.next/`.)*

The chain, each link verified independently:

1. `app/globals.css:1` is a bare `@import "tailwindcss"` with **no** `@source`
   directives and **no** `source(...)` modifier, so Tailwind v4.3.3's automatic
   source detection is in force.
2. Automatic source detection scans the whole project, excluding only paths
   matched by `.gitignore`.
3. `git check-ignore .planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-10-SUMMARY.md`
   exits **1** — `.planning/` is committed and therefore scanned. (`.gitignore`
   excludes `.ds-sync/`, `ds-bundle/`, `.design-sync/.cache/`,
   `.design-sync/learnings/` and `.playwright-mcp/`. It does not exclude
   `.planning/`, `.claude/`, or the rest of `.design-sync/`. Dot-directories are
   *not* skipped by the scanner — CR-02 proves this empirically.)
4. Tailwind treats the backticked class in the prose as a real utility candidate
   and emits `max-height: min(20rem, var(--radix-...-available-height))`.
5. `...` is not a valid CSS ident. Lightning CSS raises `Unexpected token Delim('.')`.
6. `app/globals.css` fails to load; `app/layout.tsx` imports it at line 3; every
   route throws.

The *legitimate* class this prose describes lives at
`app/(dashboard)/components/venue-switcher-menu.tsx:113` and is correct — it
names `--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height` in full. Nothing in the
application code is wrong. The document is the input.

**Fix — and which half is the band-aid.**

Editing `01.1-10-SUMMARY.md` is the band-aid. **Do not ship only that.** It
leaves the project one prose snippet away from the identical outage, and
`.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/` alone holds 33 files of exactly
this kind of writing. CR-02 proves it has already happened twice more. Fixing the
document treats the symptom; the defect is that the compiler's input set is the
whole repository.

The real fix constrains Tailwind's scan. **Adding bare `@source` lines is not
sufficient** — in Tailwind v4 an `@source` directive *adds* to automatic
detection, it does not replace it. You must either disable automatic detection
or explicitly exclude:

```css
/* app/globals.css — preferred: closed allowlist, fails closed. */
@import "tailwindcss" source(none);

@source "./";              /* app/  — this file's own directory */
@source "../components";
@source "../lib";
@source "../actions";
```

or, keeping automatic detection, the v4.1+ negative form (`tailwindcss@4.3.3` is
installed, so it is available):

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@source not "../.planning";
@source not "../.claude";
@source not "../.design-sync";
@source not "../supabase";
@source not "../README.md";
@source not "../AGENTS.md";
```

`source(none)` is strongly preferred. The `@source not` list fails **open** — the
next documentation directory anyone adds is scanned by default and nobody will
remember to come back here.

Apply the same treatment to `.design-sync/tailwind-entry.css`, which already
declares four `@source` directives (lines 20-23) *on top of* a bare
`@import "../app/globals.css"` — those are additive too, so that build also
scans the whole repo.

Then, and only then, correct the prose in `01.1-10-SUMMARY.md`.

### CR-02: Tailwind's compiler input is strictly broader than every quality gate that polices it — invalid and off-contract CSS is already shipping

**Files:** `app/globals.css:1`, `tests/theme/design-system-discipline.test.ts:72`, `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts:58`, `.design-sync/tailwind-entry.css:20-23`

**Issue.** CR-01 is not a one-off. I extracted every arbitrary-value utility
actually present in the generated CSS under `.next/` and traced each back to a
tracked file with `git ls-files`. Seven have **no origin anywhere in `app/`,
`components/`, `lib/` or `actions/`**:

| Emitted rule (brackets neutralised) | Real origin |
|---|---|
| `.rounded-[ELLIPSIS] { border-radius: … }` | `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-05-SUMMARY.md:213` |
| `.text-[SIZE] { font-size: .8rem }` | `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-05-SUMMARY.md:219` |
| `.max-w-[W28] { max-width: 28rem }` | `.design-sync/NOTES.md:98` |
| `.w-[W22] { width: 22rem }` | `.design-sync/conventions.md:51` |
| `.max-w-[W30] { max-width: 30rem }` | `.design-sync/previews/VenueForm.tsx:4,10` |
| `.w-[W26] { width: 26rem }` | `.design-sync/previews/Badge.tsx:46` |
| `.h-[H19] { height: 19rem }` | `.design-sync/previews/DropdownMenu.tsx:16`, `Toaster.tsx:13` |

*(ELLIPSIS = one U+2026 HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS character; SIZE = `0.8rem`;
W28/W22/W30/W26/H19 = `28rem`/`22rem`/`30rem`/`26rem`/`19rem`.)*

Three consequences, in descending severity:

1. **Invalid CSS is in the production stylesheet right now.**
   `.rounded-[ELLIPSIS]{border-radius:…}` is a semantically invalid declaration
   emitted from a *sentence in a planning document*. It survives Lightning CSS
   only because U+2026 happens to be a legal CSS ident character where the three
   ASCII dots in CR-01 are not. That is luck, not a boundary.

2. **A planning document is injecting a typography-contract violation.**
   `.text-[SIZE]{font-size:.8rem}` is a 12.8px font-size utility. The phase's
   entire typography thesis — `app/globals.css:99-124`, `components/ui/tag.tsx:49-53`,
   `app/tokens/primitives.css:87-102` — is that there are **exactly four size
   roles and no fifth**, and that raising the imported system's sub-14px sizes is
   the accessibility fix at the root (`lib/allergens.ts` makes the affected
   surface legally load-bearing). A fifth size is now compiled into the
   stylesheet, available to any `className` in the app, from prose.

3. **The gate that exists to catch this is structurally blind to it.**
   `tests/theme/design-system-discipline.test.ts:72` declares
   `const SCANNED_DIRS = ["app", "components", "lib"]`;
   `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts:58` declares the same three. Both
   tests are otherwise excellent — they carry explicit non-vacuity guards and
   argue against narrowing their own scope. But they police three directories
   while the compiler consumes the repository. **Any rule those files enforce
   can be bypassed by writing the offending class into a markdown file**, and the
   suite stays green. That includes the raw-hex ban, the four-role type ban, and
   the touch-floor table derived in `tests/theme/touch-targets.test.ts`.

`.design-sync/previews/*.tsx` is a design-bundle preview directory that ships
nothing; its utilities are nonetheless inflating the CSS every diner downloads,
which cuts against the DINE-03 payload constraint CLAUDE.md makes load-bearing.

**Fix.** CR-01's `source(none)` allowlist closes all three consequences at once,
because it makes the compiler's input set *identical* to the gates' scanned set.
After applying it, pin the alignment so it cannot drift again:

```ts
// tests/theme/design-system-discipline.test.ts
it("Tailwind's source set matches this gate's scanned set", () => {
  const globals = readFileSync(join(REPO_ROOT, "app/globals.css"), "utf8");

  // Automatic source detection must be OFF. It is what let a planning document
  // compile a font-size utility into the shipped stylesheet, and an invalid
  // border-radius alongside it, while this file stayed green.
  expect(
    globals,
    "app/globals.css must import Tailwind with source(none). Without it, " +
      "Tailwind scans the whole repository and every rule this file enforces " +
      "can be bypassed by writing the class into a markdown file.",
  ).toMatch(/@import\s+["']tailwindcss["']\s+source\(none\)/);

  const declared = [...globals.matchAll(/@source\s+["']([^"']+)["']/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
  expect(new Set(declared)).toEqual(new Set(["./", "../components", "../lib", "../actions"]));
});
```

Then remove the two offending literals from `01.1-05-SUMMARY.md:213,219` and
`01.1-10-SUMMARY.md:28`, or rewrite them so they are no longer valid candidates.

## Warnings

### WR-01: `useTheme()` is called with no `ThemeProvider` mounted — toasts silently follow the OS colour scheme, which this phase explicitly forbids

**Files:** `components/ui/sonner.tsx:3,64`; `app/layout.tsx:68-80`

**Issue.** `sonner.tsx:64` reads `const { theme = "system" } = useTheme()`.
`next-themes` is in `package.json`, but a repo-wide grep for
`next-themes|ThemeProvider|useTheme` across `app/`, `components/` and `lib/`
returns exactly two hits, and both are the import and the call in this one file.
**There is no provider anywhere in the tree** — `app/layout.tsx` renders
`<html>` → `<body>` → `{children}` with nothing in between.

Without a provider, `useTheme()` returns the default context, `theme` is
`undefined`, the destructuring default applies, and `<Sonner theme="system">`
ships. Sonner's `"system"` mode resolves through
`window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")`.

That is precisely the mechanism three separate contract comments in this phase
forbid:

- `app/globals.css:12-15` — *"Dark is CLASS-BASED and stays that way — keyed off
  a `.dark` ancestor, never off a media query on the operating system's colour
  preference. Auto-darkening would silently invalidate every ratio measured in
  the SC4 contrast sweep."*
- `app/tokens/cena.css:97-100` — *"No media query on the operating system's
  colour preference may ever appear in this file."*
- `app/tokens/venue.css:53-57` — rule 5, the same prohibition, extended to *"any
  stylesheet under `app/`"*.

On an owner's machine set to dark mode, sonner applies its own dark chrome to the
toast — the background, shadow, close-button and border defaults that the `style`
block at lines 77-101 does not fully override — against a light application. That
pairing appears in no row of `CONTRAST_PAIRS` (`lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts:172-296`)
and has been measured by nothing.

**Fix.** Pin it rather than mounting a provider for a dark mode this phase has
deliberately not built (`app/tokens/cena.css:76-104` argues at length why the
dark ramp must not be invented):

```tsx
// components/ui/sonner.tsx
const Toaster = ({ ...props }: ToasterProps) => {
  // NOT next-themes. D-10 wires no dark UI in this phase and the Cena dark ramp
  // does not exist yet; `theme="system"` resolves through prefers-color-scheme,
  // which app/globals.css:12-15 forbids because it invalidates every ratio the
  // SC4 sweep measured. Revisit only when the dark ramp lands AND its pairs are
  // in CONTRAST_PAIRS.
  return <Sonner theme="light" className="toaster group" /* ...unchanged... */ />
}
```

and drop `next-themes` from `package.json`, since nothing else imports it.

### WR-02: `select.tsx` and `tooltip.tsx` animate straight through `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`

**Files:** `components/ui/select.tsx:115`, `components/ui/tooltip.tsx:79`
**Contrast with:** `components/ui/dialog.tsx:84,106`, `components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx:84,283`

**Issue.** `app/tokens/primitives.css:106-116` states the contract:

> *"Motion is an accessibility surface, not decoration: honour the user's stated
> preference by zeroing the durations at the token layer, so every consumer
> inherits it and no individual component has to remember."*

`dialog.tsx` and `dropdown-menu.tsx` honour it twice over — they consume
`duration-(--duration-base)`, which the media query at `primitives.css:111-116`
zeroes, *and* they carry `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

`select.tsx:115` and `tooltip.tsx:79` do neither. `select.tsx` hardcodes
`duration-100` — a literal, immune to the token override — and carries
`data-open:animate-in data-open:zoom-in-95 data-closed:animate-out
data-closed:zoom-out-95` with no `motion-reduce:` guard. `tooltip.tsx:79` carries
the same enter/exit set plus four `slide-in-from-*` variants and specifies no
duration at all.

The token-layer claim is therefore false as written: reduced motion is honoured
by two of the four animated primitives. A user who has asked their OS to stop
animation still gets zooming selects and sliding tooltips.

**Fix.**

```tsx
// components/ui/select.tsx:115 — replace `duration-100`, add the guard
"... duration-(--duration-base) motion-reduce:animate-none data-[align-trigger=true]:animate-none ..."

// components/ui/tooltip.tsx:79 — add both
"... duration-(--duration-base) motion-reduce:animate-none data-[side=bottom]:slide-in-from-top-2 ..."
```

Then make it enforceable, so the next primitive cannot opt out silently. The
check belongs in `tests/theme/design-system-discipline.test.ts`, which already
walks `components/`:

```ts
it("every primitive that animates also honours prefers-reduced-motion", () => {
  const offenders = sourceFiles.filter(
    (f) => /\banimate-(in|out)\b/.test(f.source) && !/motion-reduce:animate-none/.test(f.source),
  );
  expect(
    offenders.map((f) => f.path),
    "app/tokens/primitives.css:106 claims reduced motion is honoured at the " +
      "token layer for every consumer. These primitives opted out.",
  ).toEqual([]);
});
```

### WR-03: `button.tsx` uses `transition-all` on a transform, contradicting the motion contract it is supposed to anchor

**File:** `components/ui/button.tsx:46`

**Issue.** The base cva string contains both `transition-all` and
`active:not-aria-[haspopup]:translate-y-px`. `app/tokens/primitives.css:68-71`
states the opposite rule, and names this exact hazard:

> *"One transition shorthand for every control, so a re-skin cannot drift
> hover/press timing per primitive. **Colour properties only** — transitioning
> geometry on a control causes layout jank on the DINE-03 critical path."*

`transition-all` transitions every animatable property including the
`translate-y-px` press offset — the geometry the token comment names. It is also
ungated by `motion-reduce:` (see WR-02) and does not consume
`--transition-control`, which is dead precisely because nothing uses it (IN-02).

Every button in the product ships this, and `Button` is the phase's canonical
primitive that nineteen other files were migrated to match — so it is the file
most likely to be copied.

**Fix.**

```tsx
// components/ui/button.tsx:46 — colour only, per app/tokens/primitives.css:68-71
"group/button inline-flex min-h-11 ... transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none outline-none ..."
```

If the press offset should still animate, name it explicitly rather than using
the wildcard:
`transition-[color,background-color,border-color,box-shadow,translate]`.

### WR-04: `<html lang="en">` is hardcoded in a product whose diner surface ships three languages

**File:** `app/layout.tsx:75`

**Issue.** The root layout pins `lang="en"` for the whole document tree.
`lib/diner-copy.ts:114-288` already ships every diner string in `hu`, `en` and
`ro`, and `lib/allergens.ts:48-88` declares the full Annex II vocabulary in the
same three — allergen labels, which PROJECT.md and CLAUDE.md both make legally
load-bearing.

When Phase 2 renders `/menu/[slug]/[lang]` under this root layout, a Romanian or
Hungarian menu will be announced by assistive technology with English phoneme
rules. For "olajos magvak" (nuts) or "crustacee" (crustaceans) — the two
categories a diner is most likely to be listening for — that is a mispronounced
allergen, not a cosmetic defect. It also fails WCAG 2.1 SC 3.1.1 (Language of
Page), which sits alongside the SC 1.4.3 gate this phase built an entire engine
for.

The route shape is already decided (`lib/diner-copy.ts:58-67`: one static page
per `(venue, language)` at `/menu/[slug]/[lang]`), so the value is available at
prerender.

**Fix.** Either move `<html>` into per-group layouts, or set it from the segment.
Minimum viable for this phase — record the constraint so Phase 2 cannot inherit
it silently:

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
<html
  // OWNER SURFACES ONLY. lib/diner-copy.ts ships hu/en/ro and lib/allergens.ts
  // carries the Annex II vocabulary in all three; a diner page rendered under
  // this value announces Romanian and Hungarian allergen names with English
  // phonemes (WCAG 2.1 SC 3.1.1). DINE-03's /menu/[slug]/[lang] route MUST set
  // its own lang — via a nested layout, or by lifting <html> out of here.
  lang="en"
  /* ...unchanged... */
>
```

and add the corresponding row to the Phase 2 plan.

### WR-05: Supabase error channels are discarded in three reads, contradicting the discipline enforced two files away

**Files:** `app/(dashboard)/components/VenueSwitcher.tsx:40-47`, `app/(tablet)/enable-staff-mode/page.tsx:38-43,55-62`

**Issue.** `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:69-85` states the rule and enforces it:

> *"ERROR CHANNEL BOUND, NOT DISCARDED. `data: null` arrives alongside a fault,
> so `if (!account)` on its own would bounce the legitimate owner off their own
> dashboard during a backend hiccup — the same lie CR-02 told one table over."*

`lib/venue-page-read.ts`, `lib/venue-landing.ts` and `lib/venue-authority.ts` all
exist to make that class of defect impossible. Three reads bypass the pattern:

**(a) `VenueSwitcher.tsx:40`** binds only `data`. Line 47 —
`if (!venues || venues.length < 2) return null;` — with the comment *"Also covers
the unauthenticated and error cases: no list, no switcher."* A transient
PostgREST fault therefore removes the switcher from the shell for a multi-venue
owner. Degradation is graceful, but it is the same discard the layout directly
above it calls a lie.

**(b) `enable-staff-mode/page.tsx:38`** binds only `data` on the memberships read.
On a fault, `ownedVenueIds.length === 0` and line 48 redirects the owner to `/` —
which bounces them onward to `/venues` — for a database hiccup, with no
indication anything failed.

**(c) `enable-staff-mode/page.tsx:55`** binds only `data` on the venues read.
This one is a concrete dead end: on a fault `enrollable` is `[]`, so
`EnableStaffModeForm.tsx:47` computes `singleVenue = null` and the component
renders the `<select>` branch (lines 61-82) whose only child is the
`<option value="" disabled>` placeholder. The select is `required`. **The owner
gets an enrolment form that cannot be submitted and says nothing about why** — on
the one screen that turns a tablet into a device principal.

**Fix.** (c) must change; (a) and (b) should follow for consistency.

```tsx
// app/(tablet)/enable-staff-mode/page.tsx
const { data: memberships, error: membershipError } = await supabase
  .from("venue_members").select("venue_id, role").eq("role", "owner");

if (membershipError) {
  throw new Error(
    `EnableStaffModePage: could not read the caller's memberships: ` +
      `${membershipError.code ?? "unknown"} ${membershipError.message}`,
  );
}

const { data: venues, error: venuesError } = await supabase
  .from("venues").select("id, name, currency").in("id", ownedVenueIds)
  .order("created_at", { ascending: true }).order("id", { ascending: true });

if (venuesError) {
  // A fault here renders an enrolment form with zero selectable venues behind a
  // `required` select — unsubmittable, and silent about why. The route error
  // boundary is the honest surface (UI-SPEC E6/E7).
  throw new Error(
    `EnableStaffModePage: could not read the owner's venues: ` +
      `${venuesError.code ?? "unknown"} ${venuesError.message}`,
  );
}
```

Note this route is in the `(tablet)` group, which has no error boundary — see
IN-05. Land that first.

### WR-06: `EnableStaffModeForm` renders an unsubmittable form when it receives zero venues

**File:** `app/(tablet)/components/EnableStaffModeForm.tsx:47,57-82`

**Issue.** Independent of WR-05's fault path, the component's own branching is
incomplete. `singleVenue` is `venues.length === 1 ? venues[0] : null`. The two
branches handle *exactly one* venue (hidden input) and *two or more* (select).
**Zero venues falls into the select branch**, producing a `required` control
whose only option is `disabled` — a form the owner can look at, fill the label
field of, and never submit, with no message explaining why.

The page above it guards `ownedVenueIds.length === 0` but not
`venues.length === 0`, and the two can differ: a read fault, or an `.in()` that
returns fewer rows than ids because RLS filtered them.

**Fix.** Make the empty case explicit and refuse it visibly:

```tsx
if (venues.length === 0) {
  // NOT an empty select: a `required` control whose only option is disabled is
  // a form that cannot be submitted and does not say so.
  return (
    <Alert variant="destructive">
      <AlertDescription>{COPY.errors.readFailed}</AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
  );
}

const singleVenue = venues.length === 1 ? venues[0] : null;
```

### WR-07: Dialog cancel controls stay enabled during the destructive transition

**Files:** `app/(dashboard)/venues/[venueId]/staff/components/deactivate-staff-dialog.tsx:65,97`, `app/(dashboard)/venues/[venueId]/staff/devices/components/revoke-device-dialog.tsx:66,101`

**Issue.** In both dialogs the confirm button is correctly `disabled={pending}`,
but the cancel button, the Escape handler and the overlay dismissal are not
gated. An owner who presses Confirm and then Cancel (or Escape, or clicks
outside) closes the dialog while the server action is still in flight.

The write itself is safe — `revokeDevice` / `deactivateStaffProfile` run to
completion and call `revalidatePath` (`actions/devices.ts:286`,
`actions/staff.ts:114`). The failure is informational: if the action **fails**,
`setError(result.formError ?? null)` writes into a dialog nobody is looking at,
and the owner is left believing a revoke happened when it did not. On the D-08
revoke path that is the exact incident-time question the registry exists to
answer, and `revoke-device-dialog.tsx:22-30` says so.

**Fix**, in both files:

```tsx
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={(next) => { if (!pending) setOpen(next); }}>
  ...
  <DialogContent
    onEscapeKeyDown={(e) => { if (pending) e.preventDefault(); }}
    onPointerDownOutside={(e) => { if (pending) e.preventDefault(); }}
  >
    ...
    <Button type="button" variant="ghost" disabled={pending} onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
      {COPY.revokeDevice.cancel}
    </Button>
```

### WR-08: `NameGridPinPad` leaks its press-and-hold timer

**File:** `app/(tablet)/components/NameGridPinPad.tsx:115,166-174,216-218`

**Issue.** Two problems with the same `holdTimer` ref:

1. **`startHold` overwrites without clearing.** Line 167 assigns
   `holdTimer.current = setTimeout(...)` unconditionally. A `pointerdown` on tile
   A followed by a `pointerdown` on tile B without an intervening `pointerup` —
   routine on a shared tablet where a finger slides off one tile onto another —
   orphans A's timer. It still fires and calls `setRevealed(A.id)`, revealing the
   full name of a staff member the user is no longer touching, and `endHold` can
   only ever clear the newest handle.

2. **No unmount cleanup.** `holdTimer` is never cleared when the component
   unmounts, which happens on every successful PIN entry (the
   `state.status === "success"` branch at line 182 replaces the render tree) and
   on navigation to `/unlock`.

3. **No `pointercancel` handler.** Lines 216-218 wire `onPointerDown`,
   `onPointerUp` and `onPointerLeave`. A touch interrupted by a system gesture
   fires `pointercancel`, not `pointerup`, so the timer survives.

This is the surface the file header describes as used *"standing, at speed,
one-handed, on glass"* — the conditions under which all three are normal rather
than exceptional.

**Fix.**

```tsx
function startHold(tile: StaffTile) {
  // Clear first: a pointerdown on a second tile without an intervening
  // pointerup would otherwise orphan the previous handle, and it would still
  // fire and reveal a tile the finger has already left.
  if (holdTimer.current) clearTimeout(holdTimer.current);
  holdTimer.current = setTimeout(() => setRevealed(tile.id), 450);
}

useEffect(() => {
  // The success branch above unmounts this component, so endHold() is not
  // guaranteed to run before a pending reveal fires.
  return () => {
    if (holdTimer.current) clearTimeout(holdTimer.current);
  };
}, []);
```

and add `onPointerCancel={endHold}` alongside the existing pointer handlers.

### WR-09: `field.tsx`'s `FieldError` de-duplicates on a possibly-undefined key, with loose equality

**File:** `components/ui/field.tsx:250-269`

**Issue.**

```tsx
const uniqueErrors = [
  ...new Map(errors.map((error) => [error?.message, error])).values(),
];

if (uniqueErrors?.length == 1) {
```

Three defects in five lines:

1. **`==` instead of `===`** at line 258. This is the only loose comparison in
   the entire reviewed set; the repo is otherwise strict.
2. **`uniqueErrors?.length`** — `uniqueErrors` is a literal array expression on
   the line above and can never be nullish. The optional chain reads as though it
   can, which is exactly the false signal `venue-switcher-menu.tsx:61-73`
   complains about elsewhere ("A comment is not a type").
3. **Keying the `Map` on `error?.message`** collapses every message-less error to
   the single key `undefined`. Given the declared type
   `Array<{ message?: string } | undefined>`, a validation result with three
   distinct-but-unlabelled failures renders as one — and the list branch at
   262-269 then filters them all out via `error?.message &&`, producing an
   **empty `<ul>`** inside an element carrying `role="alert"`: an announced alert
   with no content.

This component has no consumer today (the file header, lines 27-28, says so
explicitly), but plans 01.1-09..12 are named as the surfaces that would adopt it,
so the defect is on the adoption path rather than dead.

**Fix.**

```tsx
const withMessages = (errors ?? []).filter(
  (error): error is { message: string } => typeof error?.message === "string",
);
const uniqueErrors = [...new Set(withMessages.map((e) => e.message))];

if (uniqueErrors.length === 0) return null;
if (uniqueErrors.length === 1) return uniqueErrors[0];

return (
  <ul className="ml-4 flex list-disc flex-col gap-1">
    {uniqueErrors.map((message) => <li key={message}>{message}</li>)}
  </ul>
);
```

This also retires the `key={index}` at line 266 in favour of a stable key.

## Info

### IN-01: `radio-group.tsx`'s header comment is factually stale and defames the file it cites

**File:** `components/ui/radio-group.tsx:17-20`

The comment asserts:

> *"`checkbox.tsx` currently ships `after:-inset-x-3 after:-inset-y-2` — 12px and
> 8px — so it reaches only [40px]... plan 01.1-08 (which owns `checkbox.tsx`)"*

`checkbox.tsx:62` now ships `after:-inset-3.5`, and `checkbox.tsx:20` describes
that same superseded value in the **past** tense ("This file used to ship..."):
plan 01.1-08 landed. A reader of `radio-group.tsx` is told the sibling primitive
is under-floor when it is not.

**Fix.** Rewrite lines 17-20 in the past tense, matching `checkbox.tsx:20-27`.

### IN-02: Five design tokens in `primitives.css` have no consumer

**File:** `app/tokens/primitives.css:60,64,66,72-76,84`

Verified by grep across `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `actions/` and `tests/`,
excluding `app/tokens/` itself:

| Token | Consumers |
|---|---|
| `--transition-control` (72-76) | none |
| `--ease-out-soft` (64) | none outside the dead `--transition-control` |
| `--duration-slow` (66) | none |
| `--shadow-raised` (84) | none |
| `--radius-sheet` (60) | none |

`--transition-control` is the notable one: it is declared as *"One transition
shorthand for every control, so a re-skin cannot drift hover/press timing per
primitive"*, and no primitive uses it — every one writes `transition-colors` or
`transition-all` itself, which is exactly the drift the token exists to prevent
and is the mechanism behind WR-03.

`--duration-slow` being unused also means half the `prefers-reduced-motion`
override at lines 111-116 is inert.

**Fix.** Either wire `--transition-control` into the primitives (which would fix
WR-03 centrally) or delete it and `--ease-out-soft` with a note.
`--radius-sheet` is legitimately forward-looking for DINE-05 and can stay if the
comment says it has no v1 consumer, the way `app/tokens/venue.css:7-14` does.

### IN-03: Dead computation in `no-third-party-assets.test.ts`

**File:** `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts:113,130`

`const lines = source.split("\n")` is computed for every scanned file and then
explicitly discarded with `void lines;` and the comment *"Silences the unused
binding without weakening anything."* The line number is derived independently at
line 119 from the byte offset. Delete both lines rather than suppressing the
warning.

### IN-04: `createVenue` returns five echoed field values that no form reads

**Files:** `actions/venues.ts:28-37`, `components/venue-form.tsx:64-73,144`

`createVenue` builds `values` from six form fields and returns it on every error
path. `VenueForm` reads exactly one — `state.values?.name` at line 144. The other
five (`currency`, `defaultLanguage`, `enabledLanguages`, `countryCode`,
`timezone`) are held in local `useState` and survive a rejected submit
regardless, so the echoed copies are never consulted.

Harmless today, but `CreateVenueState.values` reads as a general round-trip
contract while exactly one key is load-bearing. Either consume them as initial
state or narrow the type and record why.

### IN-05: The `(tablet)` route group has no error boundary

**Files:** `app/(dashboard)/error.tsx` (exists), `app/(tablet)/` (none), `app/error.tsx` (none)

`app/(dashboard)/error.tsx:38-42` scopes itself explicitly and flags the gap:

> *"SCOPE. This covers the PAGES in the (dashboard) group... a later phase adding
> a fallible read to the layout needs `app/error.tsx` too."*

WR-05's recommended fix adds `throw` sites to
`app/(tablet)/enable-staff-mode/page.tsx`, which is outside that scope.
`app/(tablet)/page.tsx:66,86` already handles its own read faults with an in-page
`TabletError` retry card rather than throwing — a deliberate and correct choice
for a device used mid-service — but the enrolment and unlock routes have neither
mechanism.

**Fix.** Add `app/error.tsx` (mirroring `app/(dashboard)/error.tsx` without the
dashboard chrome) before landing WR-05's throws, or give the `(tablet)` group its
own boundary reusing `TabletRetryButton`.

### IN-06: `FieldTitle` emits the same `data-slot` as `FieldLabel`

**File:** `components/ui/field.tsx:175-186` vs `151-173`

Both render `data-slot="field-label"`. `fieldVariants` targets that slot at lines
111 and 113 (`*:data-[slot=field-label]:flex-auto`), so a `FieldTitle` placed
inside a `horizontal` or `responsive` `Field` silently inherits `FieldLabel`'s
flex behaviour. This matches the upstream shadcn registry, so it is not a
regression introduced here — but this file's header spends forty lines
disambiguating two same-named `FieldError` exports, and this collision is
undocumented. Add a line to the header, or give `FieldTitle` its own slot.

---

### IN-07: `app/(dashboard)/error.tsx` logs the full error object to the browser console

**File:** `app/(dashboard)/error.tsx:51-55`

`console.error("dashboard route error", error)` runs on every render of the
boundary. In production Next has already replaced `error.message` with a generic
string plus `digest`, so nothing sensitive escapes — the file header
(lines 32-36) reasons about this correctly. In development the object carries
PostgREST codes, table names and venue ids, which is the intent. Recorded so it
reads as a decision rather than a leftover; consider gating on
`process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` if console output from real owners'
browsers is not wanted.

## What was checked and found sound

Recorded so a later reviewer does not re-derive it:

- `lib/theme/contrast.ts` — WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 implemented correctly. All three
  channels pass through `linearise()`; the parser rejects 3-digit shorthand
  rather than mis-parsing it; the ratio is symmetric by construction. Both
  defects the header claims to avoid are genuinely avoided.
- `lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts` — `resolveVenueTheme` is total: every branch
  returns a `VenueThemeResult`, and the success branch is unreachable without
  every `RESOLVED_CHECKS` row clearing its threshold. `moreLegible` cannot fail
  to pick a winner.
- `lib/format/money.ts` — the `SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES` guard runs before `Intl`;
  the default-parameter lookup on an invalid currency yields `undefined` and
  falls through to the guard rather than throwing an opaque `RangeError`.
- `lib/allergens.ts` — all 14 Annex II categories present, `peanuts` distinct
  from `nuts`, order matches the regulation.
- `actions/venues.ts` — `revalidatePath("/", "layout")` is correctly placed
  *before* `redirect()`, which signals by throwing.
- `components/ui/checkbox.tsx:62` / `radio-group.tsx:70` — `after:-inset-3.5` on
  a `size-4` box computes to 16 + (2 x 14) = 44px exactly.
- `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` — no redirect loop is reachable: the `!account`
  branch asks the staff-membership question with the same predicate
  `app/(tablet)/page.tsx:69` uses, so an account-less owner falls through and an
  account-less staff principal lands on a surface that renders for them.
- `components/dashboard-nav.tsx` / `venue-switcher-menu.tsx` — both route the
  `/venues/new` static-sibling question through `lib/venue-routes.ts` rather than
  through duplicated literals, and `venue-switcher-menu.tsx:73` guards the
  `venues[0]` dereference its own comment identifies.
- `app/(auth)/components/GoogleOneTap.tsx` — the hashed-nonce binding is correct
  (raw to Supabase, SHA-256 to Google), the redirect destination is hardcoded
  rather than read from the response, and `onError` on the `<Script>` closes the
  blocked-bundle failure mode the header describes.
- No hardcoded secrets, no `eval`, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no `innerHTML`,
  no `as any`, no `@ts-ignore`, no `TODO`/`FIXME`/`HACK` anywhere in `app/`,
  `components/`, `lib/` or `actions/`. Non-null assertions appear seven times,
  all on `process.env` reads in Supabase client constructors plus one guarded
  `user!.id` at `app/(tablet)/unlock/page.tsx:50`.
